question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched control over the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced since the 20th Party Congress in 2022 when he secured a third term and term limits were eliminated, underpins the 95.7% trader consensus on "No." With the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027 expected to extend his leadership into a fourth term, no public signals of retirement, elite opposition, or health-related incapacity have emerged to suggest removal by December 2026. This stability reflects the absence of institutional mechanisms or visible challengers capable of forcing an early exit. Realistic scenarios that could still shift probabilities include abrupt health events, severe economic or external crises triggering elite realignment, or an unanticipated resignation—developments that remain low-probability given current party dynamics but could resolve the market early.

question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
description:

eventMetadata.context_description: The wide-open 2028 Democratic nomination race remains fragmented after the 2024 results, with no candidate consolidating early support and keeping implied probabilities clustered among Newsom, Ossoff, and Ocasio-Cortez. Traders price in a broad field where contenders build national visibility through fundraising, policy positioning on the economy and immigration, and early-state outreach ahead of the 2026 midterms. Ossoff has gained ground via strong Senate reelection fundraising and messaging, while Newsom’s lead has narrowed from prior highs amid scrutiny of his California record. Ocasio-Cortez draws progressive backing but faces questions on broader electability. Upcoming Senate contests and primary-state polling could create separation, though the field stays competitive without declared candidacies.
